name: Cryptogram
intro: A short path through Cryptograms: how the letter code works, then the two tricks that crack most puzzles: common short words and letter frequency.

lessons.title: The letter code
lessons.summary: In a cryptogram every letter of a saying is swapped for another, the same way throughout. Learn how the code works and make your first guess.
lessons.wrap: One swap, used everywhere, and never a letter for itself. Next: a quick rules check.

position.text: Y MCLLJ NYICP SN Y MCLLJ CYBLCP

steps.text:
A cryptogram is a saying where every letter has been replaced by a different one, using the same swap throughout. The small letters are the code; the big letters are your answers.

Here, four letters are already solved, and you can see them filled in everywhere their code letter appears.
This saying has a one-letter word, twice. In English, a one-letter word is almost always A or I.
steps.prompt: Tap the code letter of the one-letter word.
steps.wrong: Find a word that’s just one letter long.
steps.done: It’s A, and filling it in would add an A everywhere in the puzzle.

steps.prompt: Can a code letter stand for itself?
steps.explain: Never. If a code letter is R, the answer isn’t R.

units.name: Rules check
units.blurb: Four questions on the rules. Pass to unlock the tricks.

lessons.title: Cryptogram rules check
lessons.summary: Test your Cryptogram rules: how the letter swap works, one-letter words, and why a code letter never stands for itself.
lessons.wrap: Rules check passed. Now for the tricks.

steps.prompt: A code letter stands for E in one word. What does it stand for in the rest of the puzzle?
options: It can change from word to word
steps.explain: The same swap is used throughout.

steps.prompt: Tap the code letter that is almost certainly I.
steps.wrong: Look for a one-letter word. A is the other choice, so check which one fits the words around it.

steps.prompt: Can two different code letters have the same answer?
steps.explain: No. Each real letter has just one code letter. If two of your answers match, one of them is wrong.

steps.prompt: The code letter Q appears in the puzzle. Could its answer be Q?
steps.explain: No letter ever stands for itself.

lessons.title: Common short words
lessons.summary: Short words crack cryptograms open. Learn to spot THE, AND and other common words, and to use the letter after an apostrophe.
lessons.wrap: One-letter words, THE, and the letter after an apostrophe. Next: counting letters.

position.text: NJD DYGUB EHGX IYNIJDA NJD QVGC

steps.text:
After one-letter words, the best foothold is three-letter words. THE and AND are by far the most common.

A three-letter word that appears twice is very likely THE.
This saying has the same three-letter word twice.
steps.prompt: Tap the code letter that probably stands for T.
steps.wrong: Find the three-letter word that appears twice. T is its first letter.

position.text: NJD DYGUB EHGX IYNIJDA NJD QVGC

steps.text: Here’s the puzzle with THE filled in. T, H and E now show up in other words too.
steps.prompt: Why does one solved word help so much?
options: Its letters appear all over the puzzle
It doesn’t: each word is separate
steps.explain: The same code is used everywhere, so every solved letter is a clue for the words around it.

position.text: QSF’H GSOFH ZSOJ GYWGMCFR LCUSJC HYCZ YEHGY

steps.text: Apostrophes help too. A single letter after an apostrophe is usually S or T, as in IT’S or DON’T.
steps.prompt: Tap the code letter after the apostrophe.
steps.wrong: Find the apostrophe in the first word.
steps.done: It’s T, as in DON’T. Two letters after an apostrophe are often LL, RE or VE.

lessons.title: Letter frequency
lessons.summary: E, T, A, O, I and N are the most common letters in English. Learn to count code letters and use frequency to crack a cryptogram.
lessons.wrap: Count, guess, and check the words around your guess. You’re ready for a real puzzle.

steps.text: The most common letters in English are E, T, A, O, I and N. The code letter that appears most often in a puzzle is a good candidate for E or T.
Count the code letters in this saying.
steps.prompt: Tap the code letter that appears most often.
steps.wrong: Count again: one letter appears four times.
steps.done: Four times. In a saying this short, it’s very likely E, and here it is.

steps.text: With E filled in, the last word reads _E__E__.
steps.prompt: What should you do when a guess doesn’t fit?
options: Change it and try another letter
steps.explain: Guessing is part of solving. Fill in a hunch, see if the words around it start to make sense, and change it if they don’t. On BoardGameSite, two code letters with the same answer turn red.
